To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a recombinant PRVTk-/gE-/PCV2ORF2(2) vaccine was developed and tested in piglet models, and the recombinant vaccine was able to elicit both PRV and porcine circoviurs type 2 (PRV) specific humoral immune responses.
a recombinant PRVs expressing the ORF2 gene of PCV2 was generated, and it induced significant humoral immune response to both PRV antigens and PCV2 antigens in piglets.
a novel recombinant PRVTk-/gE-/Orf2(+) virus expressing PCV2 ORf2 gene could induce both PRV-specific and PCV2-specific immune responses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a recombinantly attenuated PRV vaccine against both PRV and PMWS.
the development of a recombinants PRV Tk-/ gE-/ORF 2(+) vaccine against PMWS.
the development of a new recombinant vaccine against PCV2 and PMWS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study provides the basis for the development of an effective recombinant PR vaccine against both PRV and PMWS.
PRV Tk-/ gE-/ ORF2(+) is a potential vaccine against PCV2.
the results of the study indicate that the recombinat PRV Tk-/ORF2+ is a potential vaccine against PCV2 and the recombinant pseudobacter virus is an effective vaccine against PRV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we successfully constructed a recombinant PR virus expressing PCV2 capsid protein, and the recombinant PCV2 capsided PR virus induced a significant humoral immune response to both PRV antigens and PCV2 capsides, and the lymphocyte proliferation response to PCV2 capsids could be detected in the piglets immunized by the virus, indicating that this recombinant PR could be a potential vaccine candidate for both PRV and PMWS.
we have developed a recombinant PRS Tk-/gE+/ORF2(+/+), which could be used as a potential vaccine against PCV2.
the recombinantly expressed PCV2 capsid protein was immunogenic in piglets and the recombinant PCV2 capsided protein was expressed in PRV-infected IBRS-2 cell.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the recombinants PRV TK-/gE-/ ORF2(+) and TK-/gE-/-ORF2(+/LacZ+) can be used to develop a potential vaccine against porcine circuovirus type 1 (PCV1) and PCV2.
we have generated a novel recombinant PR virus that can be used to vaccinate against both PCV-2 and PRV, two important swine pathogens.
PRV can be used as a vector to express PCV2 ORFe2 gene, and the recombinant pseudrabis virus can elicit both PRV and ORF2 humoral immune responses and lymphocyte proliferation response in pigs.
